steps_raw.instruction: Production of Crude AAV Virus Extract
Scope and Applicability: This protocol can be used to produce crude preps of AAV of any serotype.

Prepare DMEM with 10% FBS and 1% Antibiotic-Antimycotic by adding 50 mL of FBS and 5 mL of Antibiotic-Antimycotic to 500 mL of DMEM, and store at 4ºC.
Prepare DMEM with 1% FBS and 1% Antibiotic-Antimycotic
1 mg/mL Polyethylenimine, linear MW 25,000 Da (PEI)
7.3.1 Dissolve 1 mg of PEI (Polysciences 23966) in 1 mL of PBS
7.3.2	Adjust to a pH between 4 and 5 with 12 N HCl
7.3.3	Sterilize the solution by passing through a 0.22 µm filter unit;
7.3.4 Aliquot and store the solution at -20ºC.
7.3.5	Keep the working solution at 4ºC.
Methodology/Procedures:
Transient transfection of 293T cells

Seed 2 × 107 293 cells in 15 cm dishes to achieve ∼70% to 80% confluency the next morning (split confluent 15 cm plates of cells 1:2 into 15 cm plates). Cells are maintained in complete DMEM/10% FBS/1% Antibiotic-Antimycotic and split before reaching confluency by trypsinizing with TrypLE. Each plate contains 20 mL of culture medium.
To prepare crude AAV extract, one 15 cm plate is required for each virus prep.
For transfection of one 15 cm dish, prepare tube A in a 5 mL tube and tube B in a 50 mL tube
Mix A and B by vortex briefly for 5 seconds and incubate at room temperature for 10 min.
Add the mixture drop wise to AAV293 cells (3 mL of transfection mixture per 150 mm dish), and swirl the medium to disperse evenly.
Change the medium to 15 mL of DMEM/1%FBS/1% Antibiotic-Antimycotic between 12-24 hr post-transfection, and incubate the cells until 72 hr post-transfection.
At 72 hr post-transfection, cells and medium from each plate is collected using a cell scraper, and the mixture of cells and medium is transferred to a 50 mL tube.
Freeze the 50 mL tube in dry ice in an ice bucket
Thaw cell suspension at 37ºC and freeze/thaw 3 more times to efficiently lyse cells and release AAV particles into the solution (freeze for 20 minutes and thaw for 10 minutes each cycle)
Add 2.6 µl Benzonase nuclease (~500U/150 mm plate) and incubate at 37ºC for 30 min.
Centrifuge the crude AAV suspension at 3,000 × g for 10 minutes to remove any residual cell debris. Collect the supernatant into another clean 50 mL tube and discard the pellet.
Concentrate the crude AAV lysate using an Amicon Ultra-15 centrifugal filter by centrifuge at 3,000 x g.
Check progress and discard flow through as needed, then continue centrifugation until the desired volume remains in the unit (ideally <150 µL).
Remove virus from the Amicon filter and place into a clean Eppendorf tube.
Supernatant can be frozen at -80ºC or purified directly.
Clean the hood with 70% Ethanol after use.
The biohazard waste generated during the process is disposed according to the biohazard waste procedure guidelines.
Technical Information:

If a fluorescent reporter is part of the AAV design, check the transfection efficiency using an epifluorescence microscope. The transfection efficiency should be around 70-80% or higher in order to obtain high titer of AAV.
The purification process can be temporarily stopped at steps 8.1.8 or 8.1.12 when the cell and medium mixture can be kept at -80ºC.
